_note: CALIBRATION ARM, criterion E2. At p = 1/2 the copied-or-flipped sign is a
fair coin independent of the past, so the ERW IS srw in law and this recipe
must reproduce experiments/01_srw's four exactly known constants: gamma =
1/2, a0 = sqrt(2/pi) = 0.797885, omega1 = 1, a1 = -1/4. Not bit-for-bit --
the tree sampler consumes 2k - 1 uniforms per walk, srw consumes k -- so the
comparison is of the fitted constants inside their standard errors. It is
what licenses reading the other arms, which share its ladder and budget.
The "snr" rule with NO omega1 states no design constant at all: the
uninformed default 0 makes n_i flat, measured on srw to be the best of five
arms for identifying omega1 (experiments/01_srw/recipes/samples_pilot.json).
d is not stated either: models/erw.py's cost_hint supplies d = 1.
LADDER 4..4096, powers of two. Down to 4 because that is where
experiments/02_rwre's pilot, on the same srw law, needed the bottom rung to
see the a1/k correction above the noise; powers of two because |S_k| is a
staircase in k and a grid that mixes parities fits it as curvature.
BUDGET UNITS. tools/allocation.py prices a sample at scale i as i**d with d
from cost_hint, so a flat replicate here is n = 1e9 / (4 + 8 + ... + 4096)
= 122,129 samples per rung. This budget is the PILOT's starting point;
autopilot doubles it until both gates pass, and plan.py sizes the final run
from what the pilot measured.
